newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Fx controls stifle S.Africa investment - Old Mutual.
newsitem.headline: Fx controls stifle S.Africa investment - Old Mutual.

text.p: South Africa's foreign exchange controls act as a major constraint on badly-needed offshore investment, Mike Levett, chairman of the country's largest life assurer said on Monday.

"Our future growth in this country is importantly dependent on attracting foreign investors...and if they think the price of the rand is not properly determined they are going to be less prepared to bring their money in," he told reporters.
Exchange controls on residents meant it was not possible to determine the true value of the currency -- a major deterrent for investors looking to bring in dollars, mark or sterling.

"The sooner we free up exchange controls and get a rand determined properly by market forces..., even if the rand is at a significantly lower level, the sooner we will set ourselves on a proper road for high economic growth," he said.
Foreign investment was essential to achieve higher growth since South Africa could not generate sufficient savings internally.
Levett said South African savings were currently running at 16-18 percent of GDP while the country needed capital investment running in the mid-20s percent as a proportion of GDP.
"To get up to those middle 20s levels we need foreign money," he said.
The government's macro-economic strategy, unveiled in June, aims for a step advance in growth to six percent a year from 3.3 percent achieved in 1995 and 3.0 percent forecast for 1996.
